dedupe_keys.name: sitefinder uk mobile phone base station database ofcom released 2013

description: Sitefinder is the database of mobile phone base station locations in the United Kingdom that operators supplied to Ofcom's Sitefinder website. Ofcom released it in March 2013 as an XLSX spreadsheet with British National Grid and Irish Grid references, after a long legal dispute over public release under the Environmental Information Regulations. Owen Boswarva added WGS84 latitude and longitude and published it as shapefile and CSV, first on EDINA ShareGeo Open in April 2013 and, since February 2017, on the University of Edinburgh's DataShare. Each point is an antenna site with its operator, technology (2G or 3G) and, for many sites, antenna height, frequency, transmitter power and type. Coverage: the United Kingdom as reported up to about 2012. Format and access: shapefile and CSV, free of charge; the DataShare copy is under the Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and Licence, with notes on the original terms in the enclosed readme. Caveats: incomplete and out of date; no 4G or 5G; some operators withheld details. Simulation uses: historical base station locations for hazard exposure of mobile networks to flooding and storms, and for coverage and topology models where current data are closed. Related records: Ofcom transmitter parameters and OpenCelliD; the ANFR and ACMA registers are open counterparts elsewhere.
